captions.linkedin:
We built Digital Guardian because we wanted to help parents navigate the complex world of kids online. But sometimes, the things we plan least turn into what families love most. There was this one feature… nobody asked for it. We didn’t even think it would matter much. But then something happened.

It started when I realized how often I found myself sneaking peeks at my phone during family dinner. my 2-year-old daughter caught me once, looked right up from her mashed peas and said, “Mommy’s watching screen.” Ouch. That stung, but it told the truth. Then I saw the data. On average, we parents were checking our phones nearly 100 times during family meals each week. 📱😳

We knew that kind of distraction wasn’t good for us or our kids. It led to less talking, less laughing, and left everyone feeling less connected. But what could we do? Just telling ourselves to stop wasn’t working. Then our team had an idea: what if we built a gentle reminder into Digital Guardian? Something that encouraged mindful moments without shaming parents who needed a nudge.

So we tried it. The first time my daughter’s giggle broke through the usual mealtime hum, I realized how quiet everything else had been. Her words still echoed in my head: “Mommy’s watching screen.” Now, instead of being distracted by my phone, I chose to be present with her. Not perfect, not always easy, but real. And you know what? It made a difference.

Families began sharing their stories with us. About dinners where eyes met instead of screens, about conversations that went deeper because no one was half-listening. It turns out the feature nobody asked for became the tool that helped us build stronger connections.

#DigitalGuardian #DigitalParenting #DigitalSafety #ParentingTips
